lasts: One random baby dies in about a week. The same face, voice, and set can keep going.
make: Save one baby face. Do not use a real child's photo.
Keep one set in every episode.
Write four lines: a request, a pause, a complaint, a last line.
Record your own voice. Do not clone a real person's voice.
Turn the still into a talking clip and caption every line.
Turn on the AI label. Post the next episodes with the same baby.
tools: A still generator, your own voice, and a talking-photo tool.
avoid: A real child's face, a copied voice, or another channel's exact story.

lasts: A dance sound peaks in a few days. The same character can outlast the sound.
make: Use a dance clip you have the rights to, 8 to 15 seconds, one person in frame.
Use a character you made. Do not use a living person's photo.
Put the still onto the dance with a motion tool and export vertical.
Keep the same character next time.
Label the video as AI.
tools: A motion tool such as Viggle or Kling, plus CapCut.
avoid: A private person's face, or a celebrity's face, on the dance.

lasts: Number the episodes. One jump-scare dies faster than a series.
make: Put the episode number on screen from the first second.
Write about 80 words. A normal start, one wrong detail, a last line that reframes it.
Keep one narrator voice for the series.
Use three stills. Cut on the sentences.
End on the turn. Do not explain it.
Label it as AI.
tools: A still generator, your voice, CapCut.
avoid: Real people's faces, gore close-ups, and a new narrator every episode.

lasts: One myth clip can spike. The same art style lasts longer than a new god every upload.
make: Tell one event in 30 seconds, not the whole story.
Open on the conflict in the first two seconds.
Use one art style for the series.
Caption every line. Keep the voiceover clear of music.
Label it as AI.
tools: A still or video generator, your voice, CapCut.
